**Morning Brief — Saturday, August 29, 2026**
### World
- Nepal-China border flash floods: Death toll rises to ~626 in Nepal (thousands missing overall, including foreigners); glacial collapse triggered the disaster, with rescue efforts hampered by weather and new flood risks.
- Russian strike near Kyiv: Overnight attack on a warehouse triggers detonation, killing at least 27 (including a child); hundreds evacuated amid ongoing drone barrages.
- US-Venezuela oil deal: Trump announces "biggest oil deal in world history," giving the US majority control of >65 billion barrels of proven reserves via private partnership (expected to boost supply and lower prices).
- Iran war at 6 months: Iranian leaders acknowledge heavy economic toll (trade down sharply); US intensifies sanctions while Trump says he's "not in a hurry."
- Norway succession: King Harald dies; Haakon VIII takes the throne.
### Business
- Fed Chair Warsh at Jackson Hole: Signals the Fed may need to hike rates if underlying inflation fails to cool toward 2%; recent softer readings "do not tell me that underlying trends have meaningfully improved."
- Venezuela oil pact details: Deal (with interim President Delcy Rodríguez) could unlock ~$100B private investment and major tax revenue for Caracas while expanding US access.
- Other: Iranian economy under pressure from war/sanctions; prediction-market regulatory developments and insider-trading cases continue.
### Tech
- AI safety & policy: Judge blocks Pentagon blacklisting of Anthropic (rules supply-chain risk designation illegal); major firms (OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft, AWS +100 others) warn of limited window to prepare for AI-enabled cyberattacks.
- Hardware/AI buildout: a16z launches $1.1B "Machine Age" fund focused on physical AI infrastructure.
- Devices: Samsung unveils Galaxy Z TriFold (multi-folding phone with large screen) amid intensifying competition.
- Other: Windows 11 WinUI goes open-source; various model releases and pricing moves in the open/closed AI space.
### Overnight / Recent Market Moves
US markets closed Friday modestly lower after Warsh's hawkish-leaning remarks boosted rate-hike odds (~58% chance of September hike priced in). S&P 500: –0.2% to 7,711.76. Dow: –0.02% to 53,559.99. Nasdaq: –0.5% to 26,402.42. Week still finished modestly higher. Crypto mixed/lower.
### Weather (NYC metro)
Sunny, high 80–81°F, low 64–68°F, near-zero rain.
One story worth reading in depth: the US-Venezuela oil deal.

**Morning Brief — Monday, September 28, 2026** *(compiled late Sunday, Sept 27 EDT)*
### World
- US–Iran: Trump rejects Tehran's plan for a week-long pause to reopen the Strait of Hormuz; Iran says diplomacy is not over and its forces are ready if fighting resumes.
- UK air base: Five men arrested near RAF Fairford (used by US forces) on suspicion of explosives/terrorism offenses; Trump said they were looking to do "big damage."
- Ukraine: Russian strikes kill civilians and hit Kyivstar HQ plus other comms/data sites; exchange of fire also reported in Belgorod.
- Serbia: President Vučić resigns to run for prime minister; Ana Brnabić becomes acting president ahead of early elections.
- Switzerland: Voters reject a tighter-neutrality initiative that would have limited sanctions and NATO cooperation.
- Other: Cape Town/Johannesburg mass shootings; Saudi strike on a Taiz market; pandas Ping Ping and Fu Shuang arrive in Atlanta after the Xi visit.
### Business
- Oil & bonds: Oil bid higher after the Hormuz rejection (WTI ~$93, Brent ~$106 in Sunday trade); Treasuries resume selling, 2-year ~4.90%, 10-year still above 5%.
- US–China: Product lists out for a ~$30B tariff-cut package; sides also agreed to an AI dialogue after last week's summit (no full trade breakthrough).
- Calendar: US manufacturing Thursday; September jobs Friday.
### Tech
- AI safety: Fresh reports of model/agent mishaps (including OpenAI systems touching US government sites); Trump meets Anthropic's chief as breach/safety anxiety rises.
- Policy: China and the US agree to an AI dialogue alongside the tariff cuts.
- Infrastructure: Investor focus stays on chips, power, and data-center buildout; AI names helped Friday's close.
### Markets
Friday close (Sept 25), the first winning week in three: S&P 500 7,743.41 (+0.5% Fri, +1.2% week) · Dow 51,828.62 (+0.9%) · Nasdaq 27,068.72 (+0.5%, +2.1% week). Sunday night futures slightly lower (~–0.2%) as oil jumped and yields firmed.
### Weather (NYC metro proxy)
Nor'easter leftover: rain overnight into Monday morning, high ~64–66°F, low ~58–62°F, breezy N/NE winds. Clearing Tuesday (~70°F). Coastal flood statement in effect.
Worth reading in depth: Trump's rejection of the Hormuz ceasefire offer. Iran is treating the public "no" as unofficial until mediators deliver a formal answer.

verbatim:
Model releases, research, funding, and policy developments dominated the last ~24 hours (centered on August 28–29, 2026).
### Model Releases
- Alibaba released Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, a 125B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model (previewing Qwen4 architecture) with roughly 6B active parameters per token, a 1M-token context, and claimed training costs about one-ninth those of prior versions.
- Meta released Muse Glimmer, a 30B open-weight dense model designed to run on a single consumer GPU.
- Tencent released the Hy4 preview, a 770B open-weights MoE model (≈49B active parameters) with a 1M-token context under a permissive license.
- Z.ai published GLM-5.3 weights (753B MoE coding-focused model) on Hugging Face after a delay for risk review.
### Notable Research
- Anthropic published results on an Automated Alignment Researcher (a Claude-based agent system) that autonomously identified and fixed all 10 tested alignment failures, outperforming or matching experienced human safety researchers on most in far less time.
- LAION released the Big Video Dataset (BVD) containing ~80 million videos / 10 million hours of footage (with auto-descriptions).
### Funding & Deals
- Andreessen Horowitz raised a $1.1 billion "Machine Age Fund" focused on AI infrastructure.
- Lambda secured $1 billion in debt financing to purchase Nvidia chips for leasing (notably to Microsoft).
### Policy & Related Developments
- A federal judge ruled the Pentagon's designation of Anthropic as a supply-chain risk unlawful (First Amendment retaliation and arbitrary action), restoring eligibility for U.S. government business.
- OpenAI announced it will wind down its model-access contract with Cursor (ending direct access around November 12) following SpaceX's acquisition of the coding startup.
